2026 Arbor Day Tree Planting with Foster Dual Language School

## Arvada holds 40th annual Arbor Day tree planting celebration with Foster Dual Language School

The City's Forestry Team was joined by Foster Dual Language School fifth grade students on Monday, May 18, 2026 for Arvada's annual Arbor Day tree planting celebration. Together City staff and students planted 12 trees at Columbine Park (6710 W. 53rd Ave.).

Arvada has a long history of prioritizing its tree care, as the City earned Tree City USA recognition from the Arbor Day Foundation for the 35th consecutive year in 2026. For the sixth straight year, the City earned the Arbor Day Foundation’s Tree City USA Growth Award for its outstanding commitment to sustainable urban forest management.

Tree City USA is a partnership between the Arbor Day Foundation, the U.S. Forest Service and the National Association of State Foresters.

Arvada has earned its Tree City USA recognition by meeting the program's four requirements: maintaining a tree board or department, having a tree care ordinance, dedicating an annual community forestry budget of at least $2 per capita, and hosting an Arbor Day observance and proclamation.

Arvada’s forestry budget far exceeds the minimum criteria, as the City spends $8.35 per capita on its tree care.

The Arvada City Council signed a proclamation officially designating April 21, 2026 as Arbor Day in the City of Arvada.

## History of Arvada's Arbor Day tree planting celebration

The City's annual Arbor Day tree planting celebration began with Peck Elementary in 1987. The City partnered with Peck fifth graders each spring for 37 years until 2023, when Peck closed. During the 37 years with Peck, more than 1,800 students helped plant nearly 500 trees with Arvada park employees throughout the community. [Watch this video to learn more about the history of the Arbor Day tree planting tradition with Peck](https://youtu.be/P-3SuFkKJF8?feature=shared).
